<p class="MsoNormal">**Requirements**</p>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000">You need an Azure
subscription. If you don't have one, go to azure.microsoft.com/free and set one
up, new accounts get a free credit for the first 30 days.</span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal">**Create a resource
group**</p>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000">First, In the search
bar, type Resource groups and open that page. </span></p>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Click + Create 

- Fill in:Subscription, your subscription
     Resource group; something like rg-foundry-learning.
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Region: pick one close to you, for example
     Sweden Central.
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Click Review + create, then Create.
</ul>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000;mso-no-proof:yes"><img width="602" height="320" src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Pasted screenshot"></span><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000"></span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal">**Create the foundry
resource**</p>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Open the Azure portal and search for
     Foundry
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Go to portal.azure.com and sign in.
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Click the search bar at the top of the
     page and type Microsoft Foundry.
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Under "Marketplace" in the
     results dropdown, look for the tile with publisher: Microsoft and type:
     Azure Service.
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Select Microsoft Foundry
</ul>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000">You can also skip the
search and paste this directly into your browser: *portal.azure.com/#create/Microsoft.CognitiveServicesAIFoundry*. <br>
It drops you straight onto the form for the next step.</span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000;mso-no-proof:yes"><img width="602" height="403" src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Pasted screenshot"></span><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000"></span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000"> </span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal">**Fill in the Foundry
resource creation form.**</p>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000">Back on the Microsoft
Foundry marketplace page  click Create. You land on a creation blade
with tabs across the top: </span></p>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Basics 

- Storage

- Inbound Networking

- Outbound Networking

- Identity

- Encryption

- Tags

- Review + create
</ul>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000">On the Basics tab,
fill in:</span></p>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Subscription, same one you used for the
     resource group
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Resource group: select the one you just
     created.
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Region: match the region you picked for
     the resource group.
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Name: has to be globally unique across
     Azure, since it becomes part of your resource's endpoint
     URL. Something like foundry-yourname-learning.
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
-  Default project name: Microsoft
     folds "create your first project" into this same form. Type
     something like foundry-xx-learning for now.
</ul>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000;mso-no-proof:yes"><img width="601" height="459" src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Pasted screenshot"></span><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000"></span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000">Leave the rest at
their defaults for this first resource </span></p>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Storage , a storage account gets created
     automatically if you leave this blank.
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
-  Inbound Networking , defaults to
     public access (key or Entra ID authenticated).
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
-  Outbound Networking , default is
     fine.
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
-  Identity, default is fine.
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Encryption, Microsoft-managed keys by
     default.
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Tags are optional, skip for now.
</ul>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000">Foundry resources bill
pay-as-you-go for what you actually use.<br style="mso-special-character:line-break">
<br style="mso-special-character:line-break">
</span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal">**Review and create**</p>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Click Review + create.  Wait for the
     green "Validation passed" banner.
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Click Create.
</ul>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000;mso-no-proof:yes"><img width="602" height="594" src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Pasted screenshot"></span><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000"></span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000"><br>
Deployment takes one to two minutes. It's provisioning a resource of type
Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts .When it finishes you'll see "Your
deployment is complete", with a button "Go to resource".</span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000;mso-no-proof:yes"><img width="602" height="351" src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Pasted screenshot"></span><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000"></span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal">**See what you got**</p>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
-  Click Go to resource
     first. This opens the resource's Overview page in the regular Azure
     portal, where you'll find information about The resource's Endpoint
     URL ETC and Standard Azure controls 
</ul>

<ul style="margin-top:0cm" type="disc">
- Click Go to Foundry portal .This takes you
     to ai.azure.com. 
</ul>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000">In the upper-left
corner you'll see the project name you typed in Step 3 already selected,
because creating the resource created that project too.</span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000;mso-no-proof:yes"><img width="602" height="271" src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Pasted screenshot"><img width="601" height="186" src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Pasted screenshot"></span><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000"></span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000">That's it ,you have a
live Foundry resource with a project!</span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal"><span style="mso-ansi-language:#2000"> </span></p>
